area: test-suite effectiveness, part 2: weapon feel numbers were unprotected, and two loopback tests were load-fragile

find.report_claim: cycle 170's mutation sweep found two unprotected gameplay constants and fixed them; the sweep covered sim constants but not the weapon/enemy DATA a designer edits
find.live_evidence: a data sweep over weapons.json and enemies.json caught every outcome number (pulse damage 12->20, mite hp 30->45, mite damage 8->20, mite score 10->500) but two FEEL numbers survived: pulse kick_deg 0.6->1.2 and pulse reload_s 1.1->2.4
find.consumer_evidence: existing coverage cannot catch them because it reads the value back out of the same data: test_reload_dip.py computes half the reload as reload_s / 2.0 (correct at any duration) and test_viewmodel_recoil.py asserts sim.kick > 0.0 (true at any magnitude)

read: the loopback fixtures in the two keystone HTTP suites
killed: asserting kick_deg or reload_s as constants: it restates the data instead of asserting what the player experiences
asserting an exact frame count for the reload: a one-frame rounding difference would fail for no design reason
leaving the 5s loopback timeouts: a loaded machine is an order of magnitude slower, so those bounds turn contention into false failures
analyze.survivor: assert the observable result -- frames until the magazine refills, degrees the camera tilts per shot -- inside a design band, and give loopback requests a bound sized for a loaded machine while keeping the server-thread join tight

fix.shooter: tests/test_weapon_feel.py (4 tests) asserts a pulse reload completes in 58-74 frames (designed 66), one shot tilts the camera 0.45-0.75 degrees (designed 0.6), recoil decays back to exactly 0, and the magazine refills to its declared size; both keystone HTTP suites replace the hardcoded timeout=5 with REQUEST_TIMEOUT=60 and keep the server-thread join at JOIN_TIMEOUT=10 so a real hang still fails fast

shooter.data_sweep: 5 outcome mutations caught, 2 feel mutations survived before the fix
shooter.after: both feel mutations are caught: kick by test_one_shot_tilts_the_camera_by_under_a_degree, pulse reload by test_a_pulse_reload_takes_about_one_second
shooter.mutation_method_bug: my first reload check reported SURVIVED because I patched 'reload_s': 1.6 -- which is LANCE's value, not pulse's 1.1 -- so the mutation never touched the weapon under test; anchoring on pulse's own block made the test fail as intended, and the data file was byte-identical afterwards
shooter.flaky_under_load: under the concurrent worker's load the gate's test run failed two loopback tests that pass in isolation (7.4s and 10.1s alone), because urlopen had a 5s bound while the whole suite ran 10x slower
shooter.after_timeout_fix: the same gate run under the same load passed 5/5, with the test phase at 470s and mechanics at 91s
